updates.previous: 10% cash equity injection, 10% seller note on full standby, 80% SBA loan. Target a business priced $500K–$1.5M.
updates.proposed: At least one lender now requires 15% cash equity injection for acquisitions over $500K and will not count any seller note (full standby or otherwise) toward that requirement. Verify whether your chosen lenders still accept the 10% + seller-note structure before building deal math around it. If the 15% requirement applies, the seller note no longer halves real cash-to-close and must be treated as additional subordinated debt only.
updates.reason: New lender guidance directly contradicts the core financing assumption that a full-standby seller note covers half the equity injection. This changes required cash-to-close materially for deals above $500K.

updates.previous: $50K–$150K (scales with deal size; $100K on a $1M deal)
updates.proposed: If lender requires 15% cash (no seller note credit): $150K on a $1M deal, $90K on a $600K deal. The seller note becomes subordinated seller financing only, not an equity injection substitute. Recalculate deal size ceiling accordingly.
updates.reason: 15% cash-only injection replaces the 10% cash + 10% seller note structure for above-$500K deals at this lender.

updates.previous: Minimum $65K–$80K all-in for sub-$600K deal; recommended $125K–$175K for $1M deal; premium $200K+ if no seller note available.
updates.proposed: With $120K liquid and a 15% cash-only injection requirement: maximum supportable deal size is approximately $600K–$650K before soft costs ($120K ÷ 15% = $800K gross, minus ~$25K soft costs and ~$10K working capital reserve). The $700K–$1.5M standard target range is not executable at $120K liquid under this lender's terms. Sub-$700K deals become the primary path, not the fallback.
updates.reason: User has $120K liquid. At 15% cash injection with no seller note credit, a $1M deal requires $150K cash injection alone — exceeding available capital before soft costs. Deal size ceiling drops materially.

updates.previous: Recommended $700K–$1.5M; sub-$700K is the fallback if capital is limited.
updates.proposed: Recommended range must shift to $400K–$700K given $120K liquid and the 15% cash-only injection requirement at this lender. Confirm with a second lender whether the 10% + seller note structure is still available — if yes, a $900K–$1M deal remains possible. Do not assume the seller note structure works until a specific lender confirms it in writing.
updates.reason: User capital constraint combined with new lender guidance makes the standard $700K–$1.5M range unexecutable unless a second lender still accepts the 10% + standby note structure.

updates.previous: Seller note must be on full standby for 10 years to count toward equity injection — most sellers refuse this when they understand it means zero payments.
updates.proposed: At least one lender will not count a seller note toward equity injection at all for deals above $500K, regardless of standby terms. The full-standby seller note strategy may be lender-dependent. Confirm with each lender whether seller notes count toward equity injection before structuring any offer around them.
updates.reason: New lender guidance renders the seller-note-as-equity-injection assumption lender-specific rather than universal SBA policy.

updates.previous: Personal unlimited guarantee required for all 20%+ owners. (No note about partner refusing.)
updates.proposed: User's partner will not sign a personal guarantee. If the partner holds 20%+ ownership in the acquiring entity, the SBA requires their guarantee and the loan cannot proceed with them as a 20%+ owner. Ownership structure must be designed so the partner holds under 20%, or the partner must be excluded from the ownership entity entirely. Confirm structure with transaction attorney before forming the acquisition entity.
updates.reason: SBA policy mandates personal guarantees from all 20%+ owners. Partner's refusal is a structural blocking constraint that must be resolved before entity formation.

updates.previous: No open question about partner guarantee or lender equity injection variance.
updates.proposed: Add two new blocking questions: (1) Will your second and third lender contacts still accept 10% cash + full-standby seller note toward equity injection for deals above $500K, or have they also moved to 15% cash-only? Answer before setting deal size ceiling. (2) What ownership percentage will your partner hold? If 20%+ and they refuse to guarantee, the acquisition entity structure must be redesigned. Resolve with attorney before any LOI.
updates.reason: Both are newly surfaced blocking constraints from new lender guidance and user facts.

updates.previous: Capital below $80K total liquid makes the standard $700K–$1.5M deal range unworkable without an equity partner.
updates.proposed: At $120K liquid with a 15% cash-only injection requirement, the $700K–$1.5M range is also unworkable. Effective deal size ceiling is approximately $600K–$650K all-in. Additionally, partner's refusal to sign a personal guarantee blocks any ownership structure giving the partner 20%+ equity.
updates.reason: User capital and partner guarantee constraint together create tighter blockers than the plan previously identified.
